title: Non-Unique Factorization in Z[sqrt(-5)]
description: Formalizes the classic counterexample to unique factorization: 6 = 2·3 = (1+√(-5))·(1-√(-5)) in ℤ[√(-5)], with both factorizations into irreducibles. Uses the norm function N(a+b√(-5)) = a²+5b² and its multiplicativity.

meta.author: Formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib
meta.assumptions: 1 sorry: irreducibility of 2 (norm factorization argument). All other results fully proved.

overview.summary: Formalizes the classic counterexample to unique factorization: 6 = 2·3 = (1+√(-5))·(1-√(-5)) in ℤ[√(-5)]. Proves both factorizations, norm computations, non-unit status of all factors, and that the factorizations are essentially different (2 does not divide 1+√(-5)).
overview.text: Formalizes the failure of unique factorization in Z[sqrt(-5)] as a counterexample showing it is not a UFD.

crossReferences.description: Parent entry proving FTA. This entry shows FTA FAILS in ℤ[√(-5)].

conclusion.summary: 172 lines, 19 declarations, 0 axioms, 1 sorry. Proves two distinct factorizations of 6, non-unit status of all factors, and essential difference of the factorizations.
